enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **b)** Describe a scene in which you watched your family house being ravaged by fire. State how this incident affected your family and suggest ways by which such accidents could be avoided.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: the evening of the fire and where I was.
2. Description of the scene: flames, smoke, neighbours, firemen.
3. Effects on my family: loss of property, shelter, school, health.
4. Ways to avoid such accidents.
5. Conclusion: a lesson learnt.

**Model composition (466 words)**

It was a hot Saturday evening in March when I stood across the road and watched our family house being ravaged by fire. I will never forget that scene, because it changed the life of my family for ever.

I had gone to the market to buy a few things for supper when I heard people shouting and saw thick black smoke rising from our quarter. As I ran back, my heart beat wildly. When I reached our street, the roof of our house was already burning. Orange flames leapt through the windows and licked the wooden doors, while the iron sheets cracked and twisted with a terrible noise. Hot ash fell like rain, and the air smelt of burning plastic and wood. Neighbours were running in every direction with buckets of water, but the fire was stronger than all of us. My mother was on her knees, crying aloud, and my little sister clung to her wrapper. The firemen arrived almost an hour later because the road was bad, and by then there was nothing left to save.

The effects on my family were heavy. First, we lost almost everything we owned: our furniture, our clothes, our school uniforms, our books and the savings my father kept in a trunk. My father, a small trader, lost the goods in his shop at the front of the house. Secondly, we had no place to sleep, and we spent two weeks in the church hall before an uncle took us in. Thirdly, I could not go to school for a month because my books and uniform had gone, and my younger brother developed a cough from the smoke. Above all, my mother fell into a deep sadness and hardly ate for days. The fire left us poor and shaken.

Later we learnt that the fire started from an electric cable that had been joined badly and overloaded with too many appliances. The man who had done the wiring years before was not qualified, and nobody had checked it since then. A single spark was enough to burn down our home.

Such accidents can be avoided. Houses should be wired by qualified electricians, and old or damaged cables must be replaced at once. Families should avoid overloading sockets and should switch off appliances before sleeping. Candles, lamps and cooking fires must never be left unattended, and children should be kept away from matches. Every home should keep a bucket of sand, water and, if possible, a fire extinguisher. Roads should also be kept wide enough for fire engines to pass, and the fire service should be called immediately when a fire starts.

Today, our house has been rebuilt, but the memory of that evening remains. It taught me that fire is a good servant but a terrible master.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Describing only the fire and forgetting to state how it affected the family or to suggest ways of avoiding such accidents (all three parts are required).
2. Suggestions that are vague ("people must be careful") instead of precise.
